title: promote-latest refuses a --version strictly older than the current latest (paired with quest-cli; backports are not a promote use case)
description: Orchestrator ruling A (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-28; being recorded in opum-doc -- cite that record by ref once it lands). Found by the LCLI-617 implementer: promoting --version 0.10.5 while latest reads 0.11.0 plans without complaint and writes a record with prior 0.11.0, which LCLI-617's rule (a prior newer than the release is refused) then refuses on BOTH resume and --rollback -- so the promotion is stranded. Both repos' comments assume promotion never moves latest backwards; neither planPromotion enforces it. Ruling: planPromotion refuses a --version strictly OLDER than the current latest, before any move, with a message naming both versions. Equal-to-latest is handled however the resume path already needs; the ruling is only about strictly older. Backports are NOT a promote use case: if one is ever needed it publishes under a non-latest dist-tag through a separate path, not built now -- the refusal message and the code comment say so, so nobody 'fixes' the refusal to allow backports. quest-cli files its twin; verdicts identical (same refuse/accept on every input, wording may differ), landed by swapping head SHAs as for LCLI-617/QCLI-391.

acceptanceCriteria.text: promote-latest.mjs planPromotion (dry run and --promote) refuses a --version strictly older than the current latest of any package it would move, before any registry write, with a message naming both versions and saying backports are not a promote use case (a separate non-latest dist-tag path, not built); a code comment says the same

The comparison uses LCLI-617 compareReleaseVersions (numeric, not lexical: promoting 0.9.0 over latest 0.10.0 is refused; 0.10.0 over 0.9.0 is not); equal-to-latest keeps its existing resume behaviour, proven by a test
quest-cli twin cited by id and both merge SHAs; verdicts confirmed identical by reading each rule by ref at the other head
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change
